questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four types of client scripts in ServiceNow?

explanation.correct: The four types of client scripts in ServiceNow are onLoad, onChange, onSubmit, and onCellEdit. 'onBefore' is not a client script type; it relates to business rule timing (before business rules). See: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/yokohama-application-development/page/script/client-scripts/concept/c_ClientScripts.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: onLoad is a valid client script type that runs when a form loads and before control is given to the user.
onChange is a valid client script type that runs when a specific field value changes on a form.
onSubmit is a valid client script type that runs when a form is submitted, saved, or updated.

source.excerpt: we're going to talk about the four different times a client script can execute

questions.question: Where do ServiceNow client scripts execute?

explanation.correct: Client scripts execute on the client's web browser. When a form loads, client scripts are loaded with the form and execute in the browser, waiting for user interaction to trigger them. See: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/yokohama-application-development/page/script/client-scripts/concept/c_ClientScripts.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Server-side scripts such as business rules execute on the application server. Client scripts run in the user's browser.
The MID Server facilitates communication between the ServiceNow instance and external resources for integrations and discovery. It does not execute client scripts.
The database server stores and retrieves data. Client scripts do not execute on the database server.

source.excerpt: Client Scripts are going to execute on the browser. So when you load a form, for example-- maybe I'm on an incident, I click on an incident number and I'm bringing up that form. Client Scripts are going to load with that form and are going to wait for something to happen.

questions.question: A developer creates a client script on the Task table and enables the Inherited checkbox. What is the effect of this configuration?

options.text: The client script will only execute on the Task table and no other tables
The client script can also execute on child tables of Task, such as Incident, Problem, and Change Request
The client script will be automatically copied as separate records to all child tables
The client script will execute on every table in the ServiceNow instance

explanation.correct: When the Inherited checkbox is enabled on a client script, the script can execute on child tables that extend the selected table. For example, a client script on the Task table with Inherited enabled can execute on Incident, Problem, and Change Request tables. See: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/yokohama-application-development/page/script/client-scripts/concept/c_ClientScripts.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: This would be the behavior if the Inherited checkbox is NOT enabled. With Inherited enabled, the script extends execution to child tables.
The Inherited checkbox does not create separate copies of the client script on child tables. The single script record executes on child tables through table hierarchy inheritance.
The Inherited checkbox only affects child tables that extend the selected table through the table hierarchy, not every table in the instance.

source.excerpt: Inherited is also very nice if you're creating a client script on a table that might have child tables. So Incident, as we see here, is not a parent of any other table. But Task is. So if I was creating this client script, and I had selected the Task table, if I had inherited turned on, it could potentially execute against the Incident table or the Problem table or the Change Request table

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Order field on client scripts are correct? (Select all that apply)

options.text: The Order field appears on the Client Script form by default
Client scripts with a lower Order value execute first
The Order field should be used when multiple client scripts of the same type exist on the same table
The Order field determines whether a client script is active or inactive

explanation.correct: Client scripts execute in order from lowest to highest Order value. The Order field should be used when multiple client scripts of the same type exist for the same table and may have conflicting logic, to control which executes first. See: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/yokohama-application-development/page/script/client-scripts/concept/c_ClientScripts.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Order field does not appear on the Client Script form by default (baseline). It must be added manually through Form Layout, Form Design, or Form Builder.
The Active checkbox determines whether a client script is active or inactive. The Order field only controls the execution sequence among multiple scripts of the same type.

source.excerpt: Use the Order field when multiple Client Scripts for the same table have conflicting logic. Execute in order from lowest to highest. And it does not appear on the Client Script form baseline.

questions.question: When a user clicks 'New' to open a new incident form, which of the following can fire during the form rendering process? (Select all that apply)

explanation.correct: When clicking 'New' to open a form, query business rules fire when the table is queried for a new record, display business rules fire as the form renders to populate the scratchpad, and onLoad client scripts fire in the browser after the form loads but before the user gets control. See: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/yokohama-application-development/page/script/client-scripts/concept/c_ClientScripts.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Before business rules fire when a record is being inserted or updated (e.g., when clicking Submit or Save), not when a new empty form is being opened for display.

source.excerpt: When I click New, that's going to send a request to the server and query the table, asking for a new incident form... that's when a query business rule could fire... as the form is rendering, a display business rule may have fired by then, as well... immediately after that display business rule, an onLoad client script could fire, as well.

subtopics: Client script types (onLoad, onChange, onSubmit, onCellEdit)

questions.question: A developer needs to highlight VIP callers when the Caller field changes on the Incident form, but only when users are viewing the Self-Service (ESS) view. Which client script configuration should the developer use?

options.text: An onLoad client script with the View field set to ESS
An onChange client script on the Caller field with the View field set to ESS
An onSubmit client script with a condition that checks the current view
An onChange client script on the Caller field with no View specified

explanation.correct: An onChange client script is required because the action must trigger when the Caller field value changes. Setting the View field to ESS restricts the script to execute only when users view the Self-Service view. See: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/yokohama-application-development/page/script/client-scripts/concept/c_ClientScripts.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: An onLoad client script runs when the form loads, not when a specific field value changes. It would not respond to changes in the Caller field.
An onSubmit client script runs when the form is submitted, saved, or updated — not when a field value changes. This would not highlight VIP callers in real time.
While using an onChange client script on the Caller field is partially correct, not specifying a View would cause the script to execute on all views, not just the Self-Service (ESS) view as required.

source.excerpt: we have onChange of the Caller field... this client script is specifically executing onChange of the Caller field when someone is looking at the ESS or self-service view. But because it's only that view, this wouldn't necessarily execute when you're on the default view, for example, or maybe another view that you created.

subtopics: Client script types (onLoad, onChange, onSubmit, onCellEdit)

questions.question: Which GlideForm (g_form) method is used to retrieve the current value of a field on a form in a client script?

explanation.correct: The g_form.getValue('fieldName') method retrieves the value of a specified field on the current form. This is the standard GlideForm API method for reading field values in client scripts and UI policies.

wrongAnswers.explanation: getFieldValue() is not a valid GlideForm method. The correct method is getValue().
g_form.get() is not a valid method for retrieving field values. getValue() is the correct GlideForm method for this purpose.
readValue() is not a valid GlideForm method. The GlideForm API uses getValue() and setValue() for reading and writing field values.

source.excerpt: I know that if I want to get the value of the impact field, say from a UI policy or a client script, I need to use this GlideForm method, getValue. Maybe add store it into a variable.

questions.question: In which type of ServiceNow script are the 'current' and 'previous' objects available for accessing record field values?

explanation.correct: The 'current' and 'previous' objects are available in server-side scripts that are associated with a table, such as business rules. The 'current' object contains the values being submitted, while 'previous' contains the values before the update. These objects are not available client-side.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Client scripts run in the browser (client-side) and do not have access to the current or previous objects. They use the g_form API to interact with form fields.
UI policies are client-side configurations and do not have access to the current or previous objects. They use g_form methods to get and set field values.
UI scripts are client-side script libraries that run in the browser. They do not have access to server-side objects like current and previous.

source.excerpt: Test number one-- are you dealing with a server-side script, like a business rule? If so, you're halfway there. There is no current or previous object available client-side.

questions.question: Why are display business rules with the g_scratchpad object preferred over GlideAjax calls when server-side data is needed at form load?

options.text: Display business rules can dynamically update data when field values change on the form
Display business rules send data along with the initial form load, avoiding an additional round trip to the server
The g_scratchpad object allows client scripts to directly query the database without server involvement
Display business rules execute asynchronously and therefore do not impact form load performance

explanation.correct: Display business rules run on the server before the form is sent to the client. By writing values to the g_scratchpad object, the data 'rides along' with the form response, eliminating the need for a separate asynchronous server call (GlideAjax). This avoids an additional round trip and improves performance.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Display business rules only fire once when the form loads. They cannot dynamically update data when field values change — that requires a GlideAjax call.
The g_scratchpad object is simply a data-passing mechanism between a display business rule and client scripts. It does not allow direct database queries from the client side.

Display business rules are synchronous server-side scripts that execute before the form is rendered. They are not asynchronous. Their advantage is that they piggyback on the existing form load request.

source.excerpt: we're saying, if you're going to be there anyway, please bring back this extra thing for me so I can avoid making a round trip. That is what display business rules in scratchpad do for us. That's why we like them.

questions.question: In which of the following server-side script types must a developer query records using GlideRecord or GlideQuery instead of relying on the 'current' object? (Select all that apply)

explanation.correct: Scheduled scripts and script includes are server-side scripts that are not directly associated with a table record operation. They do not have the 'current' or 'previous' objects automatically provided. To access records, developers must explicitly query using GlideRecord or GlideQuery.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Business rules are associated with a specific table and fire in response to record operations (insert, update, delete, query). They automatically receive the 'current' and 'previous' objects.
Script actions are triggered by events that are associated with a specific record, so they do have access to the 'current' object representing the record that triggered the event.

source.excerpt: other types of server-side scripts, like fixed scripts, scheduled scripts, script includes, in all of those, if you want to access a particular record, you're going to have to query it with GlideRecord or GlideQuery.

questions.question: A developer needs to display the Assigned To user's manager's email address in a field message on the Incident form. The email should appear when the form loads but does not need to update when the Assigned To field value changes. What is the recommended approach?

options.text: Use dot-walking in an onLoad client script to access current.assigned_to.manager.email
Write a GlideAjax call in an onChange client script to fetch the manager's email from the server
Use a display business rule to dot-walk to the manager's email and pass it to the client via g_scratchpad
Create a UI macro that queries the manager's email and renders it on the form

explanation.correct: A display business rule can dot-walk server-side to retrieve the assigned user's manager's email (e.g., current.assigned_to.manager.email) and write it to g_scratchpad. The client script then reads the value from g_scratchpad when the form loads. This avoids an extra round trip to the server since the data is sent along with the form.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Client scripts cannot use dot-walking on the 'current' object because it is a server-side object. Client scripts do not have access to 'current' or 'previous', and dot-walking to related records is not possible client-side.

While GlideAjax would work, it makes an additional asynchronous round trip to the server. Since the requirement only needs the data at form load and not dynamically, a display business rule with g_scratchpad is more efficient and the recommended approach.

UI macros are used for reusable UI components (Jelly-based) and are not the recommended pattern for passing server-side data to client scripts. The display business rule and scratchpad pattern is the standard approach for this use case.

source.excerpt: this technique, dot walking in a display business rule and writing it to the scratchpad, allows us to get this information which our client script wouldn't ordinarily be able to figure out because it involves a server call.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid Client Script types in ServiceNow? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: The four valid Client Script types are onLoad, onChange, onSubmit, and onCellEdit. onLoad executes when a form loads, and onChange executes when a specific field value changes. See: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-application-development/page/script/client-scripts/concept/c_ClientScripts.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: onDisplay is not a Client Script type. Display business rules exist server-side, but there is no onDisplay client script type.

onCellEdit is a valid Client Script type (the fourth type alongside onLoad, onChange, and onSubmit), but it was listed as a distractor in this question format. Note: onCellEdit IS actually valid — it runs when a cell in a list is edited.

references: Scripting in ServiceNow Fundamentals - Client Scripts

questions.question: A developer creates a Client Script on the Task table with the 'Inherited' checkbox enabled. Which tables will this script execute against?

options.text: Task and all tables that extend Task (Incident, Problem, Change, etc.)
Only child tables of Task, not the Task table itself

explanation.correct: When the Inherited checkbox is enabled on a Client Script, it executes on the specified table AND all tables that extend it. Since Incident, Problem, Change Request, and other tables extend Task, the script runs on all of them. See: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-application-development/page/script/client-scripts/concept/c_ClientScripts.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: With Inherited enabled, the script is not limited to just the Task table — it also runs on child tables.
The script only applies to the specified table and its descendants in the table hierarchy, not every table in the instance.
The script runs on both the parent table (Task) and all child tables. It does not exclude the parent.

references: Scripting in ServiceNow Fundamentals - Client Scripts

source.excerpt: if I was creating this client script, and I had selected the Task table, if I had inherited turned on, it could potentially execute against the Incident table or the Problem table or the Change Request table

questions.question: Multiple onChange Client Scripts exist on the Incident table's Caller field. What determines the order in which they execute?

options.text: The Order field value, from lowest to highest
Random order determined by the server

explanation.correct: The Order field controls execution sequence for multiple Client Scripts of the same type on the same table/field. Scripts execute from lowest Order value to highest. The Order field is not on the Client Script form by default and must be added via Form Layout. See: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-application-development/page/script/client-scripts/concept/c_ClientScripts.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Client Script execution order is not determined by the script name. It is controlled by the numeric Order field.
Creation date does not determine execution order. The Order field must be explicitly set to control sequencing.
Execution order is deterministic when the Order field is set. Without it, the order may be unpredictable, which is why setting it is a best practice.

references: Scripting in ServiceNow Fundamentals - Client Scripts

source.excerpt: Use the Order field when multiple Client Scripts for the same table have conflicting logic. Execute in order from lowest to highest. And it does not appear on the Client Script form baseline.

questions.question: Which Client Script type is NOT one of the four standard types in ServiceNow?

explanation.correct: The four Client Script types are onLoad, onChange, onSubmit, and onCellEdit. There is no 'onSave' type — save actions are handled by the onSubmit type, which runs when a form is saved, updated, or submitted. See: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-application-development/page/script/client-scripts/concept/c_ClientScripts.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: onLoad is a valid Client Script type that runs when a form loads before control is given to the user.
onSubmit is a valid Client Script type that runs when a form is saved, updated, or submitted.
onCellEdit is a valid Client Script type that runs when a cell in a list is edited inline.

references: Scripting in ServiceNow Fundamentals - Client Scripts

source.excerpt: the four different times a client script can execute... onLoad... onChange... onSubmit... onCellEdit

questions.question: A developer wants a Client Script to run only when users view the Self-Service (ESS) view of the Incident form. How should this be configured?

options.text: Set the Type to 'onLoad' and add a condition checking the current view in script
Uncheck the 'Global' checkbox and enter 'ess' in the View field
Create the Client Script on the Service Portal table instead
Set the UI Type to 'Mobile' only

explanation.correct: When the Global checkbox is unchecked on a Client Script, a View field appears where you can specify which view(s) the script should execute on. Entering 'ess' (the system name for the Self-Service view) restricts the script to only that view. Multiple views can be specified comma-separated. See: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-application-development/page/script/client-scripts/concept/c_ClientScripts.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: While you could check the view in script, the platform provides a built-in View field for this purpose, which is the correct approach.
The Self-Service view (ESS) is a form view on the standard Incident table, not a separate Service Portal table.
UI Type controls whether the script runs on desktop, mobile, or both. It does not control which form view triggers the script.

references: Scripting in ServiceNow Fundamentals - Client Scripts

source.excerpt: since the View checkbox is not on, it's asking, well, which view do you want it to display? ... the actual name of that view is ESS. So in this example, this client script is specifically executing onChange of the Caller field when someone is looking at the ESS or self-service view.

questions.question: A developer writes an onSubmit Client Script that returns false. What happens when a user clicks the Submit button?

options.text: The record is submitted and then immediately deleted
The form submission is cancelled and the record is not saved
The record is saved but marked as draft
An error is thrown and the page crashes

explanation.correct: When an onSubmit Client Script returns false, it cancels the form submission. The record is not created or updated in the database, and the user remains on the form. This is commonly used for client-side validation. See: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-application-development/page/script/client-scripts/concept/c_ClientScripts.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Returning false prevents submission entirely — the record is never sent to the server, so it cannot be deleted.
There is no draft mechanism triggered by returning false. The submission is simply cancelled.
Returning false is normal Client Script behavior for cancelling submissions, not an error condition.

references: Scripting in ServiceNow Fundamentals - Client Scripts

source.excerpt: the script runs when a form is saved, updated, or submitted... It's typically used for field validation

questions.question: A developer needs to make the 'Short description' field mandatory only when the Priority is set to 1 - Critical. Which client script type should they use?

options.text: onChange client script on the Priority field

explanation.correct: An onChange client script on the Priority field fires whenever the user changes the priority value, allowing you to call g_form.setMandatory('short_description', true) when priority is 1.

wrongAnswers.explanation: An onLoad script runs when the form loads, but would not respond to subsequent changes to the Priority field.
An onSubmit script runs when the form is submitted. While it could validate, it would not provide real-time feedback as the user changes Priority.
onCellEdit scripts run in list view when cells are edited, not on the standard form.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a valid g_form method for controlling field visibility?

explanation.correct: There is no setVisible() method on g_form. The correct method to hide a field is g_form.setDisplay() or g_form.setVisible() does not exist as a standard API.

wrongAnswers.explanation: g_form.setDisplay() is a valid method that controls whether a field is displayed on the form.
g_form.hideFieldMsg() is a valid method that hides a previously shown field message.
g_form.hideRelatedList() is a valid method that hides a related list on the form.

questions.question: A developer writes an onChange client script but it does not fire when the form loads with a pre-populated value. What should they add?

options.text: Set the 'Inherited' checkbox on the client script
Add an onLoad client script that manually triggers the onChange logic
Check the 'Fire on load' option in the onChange client script
Set the business rule to populate the field after form load

explanation.correct: The onChange client script has an 'Inherit' checkbox but lacks... Actually, onChange scripts in ServiceNow do not fire on initial form load by default. However, adding an onLoad script that calls the same logic is the standard workaround.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The 'Inherited' checkbox controls whether the script applies to extended tables, not whether it fires on load.
Changing when the field is populated does not solve the problem of the onChange not firing on initial load.

questions.question: Which TWO methods can be used to get the value of a field in a client script? (Choose 2)

explanation.correct: g_form.getValue() returns the actual value of a field, and g_form.getDisplayValue() returns the display value. Both are valid client-side methods to retrieve field values.

wrongAnswers.explanation: g_form.getReference() retrieves the full GlideRecord of a reference field asynchronously. While it can get values, it's specifically for reference lookups, not general value retrieval.
'current' is a server-side object available in business rules. It is not available in client scripts.
